citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: The level where a learner works on one specific task, in three phases (representing the task, processing it, and performing and evaluating), together with the experiences that arise as the work goes on. Regulation happens here, and Person-level characteristics can influence it.

examples: A student plans how to wire a flashlight and feels curious.
A student judges that the finished flashlight is correct and feels satisfied.
